requirement:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
MessagePack generated code is not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
There are no alternatives, it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases.

#### Additional context

N/A

story.summary:
Each of the six T4 templates (object, string-key, enum, union, resolver, composite resolver) now puts `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` on the types it generates, wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. The nested `FormatterCache<T>` and `GetFormatterHelper` classes in the resolvers get the attribute too. The compiled .cs counterparts are updated to match. TransformUtilities now writes a newline after `{` so the `#if` starts on its own line. 222 snapshot files are updated. The change adds a README note and a new test class with two tests.

Unrelated to the requirement, the string-key formatter template no longer emits `options.Security.DepthStep(ref reader);` or `reader.Depth--;` in Deserialize. Those two lines are the recursion-depth guard against hostile payloads.
story.why: Issue 2297 asks that all MessagePack-generated code carry ExcludeFromCodeCoverage so it does not skew coverage numbers.
touches_beyond_requirement: StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt/.cs removes the DepthStep / Depth-- security guard from generated map-mode deserializers. This is not required and weakens protection against deeply nested untrusted input.
TransformUtilities.cs line 58 adds a newline after `{` for nesting types with constraints. This is needed so `#if` lands at the start of a line; it is a formatting-only change.
README.md documents the feature and states the attribute is unavailable on netstandard2.0/.NET Framework. That statement is factually doubtful.
story.confidence_overview:
High that the attribute is emitted by every template; it is visible in each template and in the uniform snapshots (S2).

Medium on test strength. The new test checks only one occurrence per file, does not cover the composite resolver, and does not compile the generated output.

High that the DepthStep removal is real. S5 and S6 missed it. The snapshot shapes in S2 do not show the removal, so the snapshots may not match the template.

refusals.what: Generated map-mode Deserialize no longer calls options.Security.DepthStep or decrements reader.Depth.
refusals.why: This removes recursion-depth protection in code that deserializes untrusted input. It is a security-relevant change that the requirement does not ask for.

findings.description: Claim C5 disputed: The named tests do not specifically test C5's cited lines (ResolverTemplate.tt lines 14-16 and ResolverTemplate.cs line 38). Because ResolverTemplate also emits two other guarded ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attributes on FormatterCache<T> (lines 31-33) and GetFormatterHelper (lines 48-50), reverting lines 14-16 on the outer partial class would leave both AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage (CodeCoverageExclusionTests.cs line 75, checking text.Contains) and ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable (lines 91-95, checking attributeCount > 0 and attributeCount == guardedCount) passing.

Claim C9 disputed: First, the requirement ('all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute', misquoted by C9 with the sentence about settings) is needlessly only partly met: parameterless System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute has existed since .NET Framework 4.0 and .NET Standard 2.0, so #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK strips the attribute on targets where it is available. Second, the named test ExcludeAttributeIsGuardedForTargetsWhereItIsUnavailable (CodeCoverageExclusionTests.cs lines 82-97) never exercises CompositeResolverTemplate.tt (lines 7-9 and 35-37), so it does not verify every emitted attribute across all templates.

`options.Security.DepthStep(ref reader);` and the matching `reader.Depth--;` (old line near 131) are deleted. Generated string-keyed (map-mode) formatters no longer enforce MessagePackSecurity.MaximumObjectGraphDepth. A deeply nested untrusted payload can then cause a stack overflow (DoS). This is unrelated to the requirement, and S5/S6 did not catch it.

The compiled template drops the DepthStep and Depth-- writes, mirroring the .tt. S2 lists no `-options.Security.DepthStep` shape among the snapshot changes. Either the map-mode snapshots (e.g. FormatterForClassWithPrivateMembers_MapMode) no longer match what the generator emits, so snapshot tests would fail, or the snapshots were edited inconsistently.

System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute exists in .NET Framework 4.0+ and in netstandard2.0. The `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` guard is therefore unnecessary. It leaves generated code un-excluded for those consumers, contrary to 'all generated code'. The same guard is used in every template.
States the attribute is not available on netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework. This appears factually wrong (see the previous concern).

The assertion is per file (`text.Contains`). A file whose outer class is decorated but whose nested FormatterCache/GetFormatterHelper are not would still pass. The generated code is never compiled, the composite resolver is not exercised, and generator diagnostics are discarded (line 123).

Removing options.Security.DepthStep(ref reader); and reader.Depth--; (also in StringKeyFormatterTemplate.cs lines 115 and 169) disables MessagePackSecurity.MaximumObjectGraphDepth enforcement for generated map-mode (keyAsPropertyName: true) formatters with members, allowing deeply nested untrusted payloads to bypass UntrustedData depth limits and crash the process with StackOverflowException. It also leaves an empty if (Info.Members.Length != 0) block at line 131 and makes StringKeyFormatterTemplate output diverge from the un-updated string-keyed snapshot .g.cs files under Resources/.

Emitting [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on the outer partial class declaration (and similarly in CompositeResolverTemplate.tt line 8) causes compiler error CS0579 (Duplicate 'ExcludeFromCodeCoverage' attribute, since AllowMultiple is false) for any consumer who already placed [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] on their hand-written partial resolver declaration, and also excludes user-written members in other parts of that partial class from code coverage instead of decorating only the generated members and nested types.

Guarding [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] with #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK across all six templates (and documenting in README.md line 1640 and CodeCoverageExclusionTests.cs line 18 that the attribute is unavailable there) is factually wrong: parameterless System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute has been in the BCL since .NET Framework 4.0 and .NET Standard 2.0 (only the unused Justification property requires .NET 5+). Because the .NET SDK defines NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK on those targets, netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework consumers needlessly lose code coverage exclusion on all generated code.

In AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage, Assert.True(generated.Count >= 5) assumes the 5 files are MyObject, MyStringKeyObject, MyEnum, IMyUnion, and GeneratedMessagePackResolver, overlooking that MyUnionMember (line 48) also carries [MessagePackObject] and produces a 5th file by itself while MyEnum (line 37) is unattributed and unreferenced by any serialized member; if no MyEnumFormatter is generated, the assertion still passes without testing EnumTemplate.
